 사진 확대 The producer price index fell 0.1 percent in October from the previous month, according to the Bank of Korea. Citizens are looking at ingredients for kimjang at the Yangjae branch of Hanaro Mart in Seocho-gu, Seoul. Prices of agricultural, forestry and fisheries products fell 8.3%
 Producer prices fell for the first time in three months
 Imported raw material prices jumped 10.8%
 Inflationary pressure still persists 
 Producer prices fell for the first time in three months last month as prices of agricultural and livestock products such as apples and pork fell sharply. However, inflationary pressure continues, with the price of petroleum and chemical products rising and the price of imported raw materials rising by double digits due to rising international oil prices.
 According to the Bank of Korea on the 20th, the producer price index in October was 129.66 (2020 = 100), down 0.1% from the previous month. Producer prices rose 0.1% in August and September, respectively, after falling -0.4% in July, but turned downward in three months. Compared to the same month last year, it rose 7.2%, still showing a high rate of increase. However, the rate of increase has slowed for two consecutive months since August (7.9%).
 Prices of agricultural, forestry and fisheries products fell 8.3 percent from the previous month. Fisheries products (1.4%) rose, but agricultural products (-11.8%) and livestock products (-7.3%) fell sharply. Apple (-29.2%), which increased shipments due to strong weather conditions, and pork (-12.8%), which has seen a decrease in demand since Chuseok, were particularly large.
 On the other hand, the domestic supply price index, which represents the prices of domestic goods and services, including imported goods, rose 0.7% from the previous month, returning to an upward trend for the first time in four months.
 Imported raw material prices jumped 10.8 percent, pushing up raw material prices by 7.3 percent and intermediate goods also up 0.1 percent. It was analyzed that the impact of Dubai oil prices soaring 28.1% in September from the previous month in dollar terms was reflected with a time lag.
